lines.explanation: Searches for 'food' and 'eat' were run and results gathered (read-only deliverable performed). The three required whole-word matches (Kenji, Olena, Mateo) were correctly identified and later credited by name in the opening post, satisfying O2. However, the food-chatter content actually woven into downstream output (O1's referent set of exactly three qualifying messages) was expanded to include Lukas's and Sophie's espresso/French-press/pizza messages, none of which contain 'food' or 'eat' as whole words, exceeding the resolved referent scope.
The only channel flagged is_archived (C_OLD_PROJECT) was correctly identified, unarchived, renamed to midnight-bazaar, and joined by the agent so it could be used as HQ.

Topic was set on the correct (resolved) channel and textually contains 'street food' and night-market framing; the stored value shows mojibake/encoding corruption of the emoji/dash characters, a content-fidelity defect but not a referent error.

An opening post was successfully created in the correct revived channel (satisfying O3). It weaves in food discussions but exceeds the O1 referent set by folding in the non-qualifying espresso-machine/pizza-order/French-press exchange (Lukas, Sophie) alongside the three qualifying messages (Kenji, Olena, Mateo).
Mateo was correctly identified and removed from the correctly identified #project-alpha-dev channel via conversations.kick, matching the diff's channel_members deletion.

Card O6 is underspecified (four candidate espresso-machine messages), making this line inactive under rule 4. The agent nonetheless silently selected one candidate (ts 1706051580.000000, Lukas's noise complaint) without surfacing the ambiguity, an unauthorized choice constituting demonstrated_incorrect handling regardless of outcome. Every chat.update attempt against that message returned 'cant_update_message'; no edit was ever applied (no corresponding update appears in the diff), so no part of the requested edit was performed.

The correct message (ts 1706051755.000000, Mateo's 'large pies' message) was correctly identified via search, satisfying O7's resolved referent. However every chat.delete attempt against it returned 'cant_delete_message' or 'message_not_found'; the message was never deleted, and no corresponding removal appears in the diff.
